title: Clocks, Counts, Columns, Carets & Lists
description: Five jobs the platform quietly took over: split transforms, filtered counting, upright digits, a manual caret, and native lists.

drops.title: Three Clocks, One Element
drops.description: translate, rotate and scale are separate properties, so three animations can own one element at three different speeds.
drops.concept: Because translate, rotate and scale exist as properties rather than only as transform() functions, three independent animations can target the same element without any of them clobbering the others. The drop runs drift, spin and pulse together on five tiles, then repeats the exact same timings written against the transform shorthand — where the last animation simply wins and the other two vanish.
drops.source: web.dev — 'Finer grained control over CSS transforms with individual transform properties'

interaction.mouse: Hover a tile to add rotation on top of the running translate and scale without disturbing either.
interaction.click: Pause and resume every clock at once; drag the panel sliders to retune each animation independently.
interaction.touch: All five tiles animate unattended; the panel is hidden below 760px so the comparison fills the screen.

drops.title: Counting Only What's Left
drops.description: An+B of S makes :nth-child() count only the children that match the selector, so stripes survive filtering.
drops.concept: The 'of S' clause filters the child list before the An+B index is applied. Filter the 22-card grid by tag and the zebra stripes, the 'first visible' marker and the 'last visible' marker all re-index themselves with no JavaScript bookkeeping. A toggle strips the clause back out so you can watch plain :nth-child() count the hidden cards and break.
drops.source: Chrome for Developers — 'More control over :nth-child() selections with the of S syntax'

interaction.mouse: Toggle the tag chips to hide and show cards and watch the markers follow.
interaction.click: Pick a different An+B pattern (odd, even, 3n, 4n+1, -n+3) or drop the 'of S' clause to see the naive version.
interaction.touch: Filter chips and the generated-selector readout are full width; the tuning panel is hidden below 860px.

drops.title: Numbers That Stand Up
drops.description: text-combine-upright: all folds a year, a price or a chapter number into a single upright slot in vertical Japanese text.
drops.concept: Set Japanese with writing-mode: vertical-rl and every Latin digit rotates onto its side, one glyph per line. One declaration — text-combine-upright: all — compresses a short run into the space of a single character, upright, which is the typographic convention called tate-chu-yoko. Four vertical slabs show two-, three- and four-digit runs, each over a faint plate so the single square it now occupies is visible.

interaction.mouse: Read the four slabs side by side; the tinted plates mark every combined run.
interaction.click: Toggle the property off to watch the digits unstack, flip the writing direction, or switch text-orientation to upright for contrast.
interaction.touch: Slabs wrap and scroll vertically; type size, line height and tracking are panel sliders on wider screens.

drops.title: The Caret, On Your Terms
drops.description: caret-animation: manual switches off the browser's blink so your own caret-color keyframes can run uninterrupted.
drops.concept: The text cursor has always blinked on the browser's schedule, which meant any caret-color animation fought it for half of every cycle. caret-animation: manual suppresses the blink and hands the caret's colour to CSS. Four fields demonstrate a palette sweep, a soft breathe, a faster-than-default strobe and a caret that never blinks at all — with a toggle back to auto so the collision is visible.
drops.source: Stephen Chenney (Igalia) — 'Caret customization on the web'

interaction.mouse: Click into any field to put a caret there; each field animates its caret differently.
interaction.click: Flip caret-animation between manual and auto to watch the browser's blink start overriding the keyframes.
interaction.touch: Tap a field to focus it; the beat slider lives in the panel on wider screens.

drops.title: The List the Browser Already Draws
drops.description: One <datalist> gives four different controls a suggestion UI: slider ticks, a filtering combobox, colour swatches, suggested dates.
drops.concept: datalist is the oldest technique in today's five and by far the least used. Linked with the list attribute it makes a range input draw tick marks at every option value (evenly spaced or not), turns a text field into a filtering combobox that still accepts free text, seeds the native colour picker with preset swatches, and offers suggested dates. The panel rebuilds the slider's scale by editing only the option list, and switching the list attribute off makes every tick disappear.
drops.source: MDN Web Docs — '<datalist>: The HTML Data List element'

interaction.mouse: Drag either slider — the readout names the nearest notch; open the colour picker to find the seeded swatches.
interaction.click: Rebuild the tick scale from the panel, toggle option labels, or remove the list attribute entirely to watch the ticks vanish.
interaction.touch: Every control is native, so the platform's own touch pickers and keyboards apply; the panel is hidden below 900px.
